newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bond funds rise 2.08 pct in Q3 - Lipper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bond funds rise 2.08 pct in Q3 - Lipper.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income funds rose 2.08 percent in the third quarter, helped by new evidence of weakness in the U.S. economy in September, according to data from Lipper Analytical Services.
For the nine months, the average taxable bond fund gained 1.83 percent.

Emerging market bond funds rose 12.89 percent in the quarter and 29.84 percent for the nine months. International bond funds were up 3.73 percent for the quarter, and 5.02 percent for the nine months.
Total returns are calculated after dividends are reinvested, Lipper said.

High current-yield taxable funds added 4.66 percent, general U.S. government funds rose 1.52 percent for the quarter, U.S. mortgage funds gained 1.84 percents, corporate debt funds A rated were up 1.72 percent, and global income funds rose 3.98 percent.
Among municipal money market funds, tax-exempt funds increased 0.71 percent, intermediate municipal debt funds gained 1.76 percent, and general municipal debt funds rose 2.27 percent.
Money market instrument funds were up 1.18 percent, and institutional money market funds were up 1.26 percent.
